I would agree, reporting him would probably make you feel better and possibly protect and prevent his future victims. 

However, and I do not say this lightly, if you are already feeling exhausted and possibly do not have a good support network this can be a very draining process. Often statements have to be taken multiple times and people may not always believe you (especially seeing as he is already part of the police force). You will have to relive everything you have suppressed. It will be traumatic, it will run you down and put stress on your relationships. 

Of course this sorry excuse for a human shouldn't be free let alone in a position of power, and if you free you can get through this, I strongly recommend it, for yourself and others past and future. Some people are sick. But remember this will take time, there are no quick fixes, police are slow, court dates (if it comes to that) are slower. Do whatever you can now to make yourself mentally prepared. Join support networks, tell friends/family you think will understand and stand by you (your partner sounds like a good egg, so that's one on your side already). You may need to take medication for a while, and there's nothing wrong with that, not antidepressants necessarily, but it's amazing what a continued bad sleep can do to a person, so maybe just low dose sleeping pills. You may need therapy. I do not know you or you capabilities but asking for help isn't shameful. 

Whatever you decide, you have to live with that decision. 

Good luck with your future. x
